\subsection*{Space Complexity --- Exp Time: Results}

\begin{theorem}[Nondeterministic space and deterministic time]
\lean{Complexity.NSPACE_subset_exp_dtime}
\label{Complexity.NSPACE_subset_exp_dtime}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.DTIME, Complexity.NSPACE, Complexity.NSPACE_subset_exp_dtime_of_le, Complexity.SpaceConstructible}
\difficulty{1}
Let $S:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ be space-constructible: there are a positive integer $a$
and a deterministic Turing machine that computes the binary representation of $S(n)$
using at most $aS(n)$ space on inputs of length $n$, and $1+\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor\le
S(n)$ for every $n$. Then every language decidable nondeterministically in space bounded
by a constant multiple of $S$ is decidable deterministically in time bounded by
$2^{c(S(n)+1)}$ for some constant $c\in\mathbb{N}$; equivalently,
$\mathrm{NSPACE}(S)\subseteq\bigcup_{c\in\mathbb{N}}\mathrm{DTIME}\bigl(n\mapsto
2^{c(S(n)+1)}\bigr)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Nondeterministic log space is contained in polynomial time]
\lean{Complexity.NL_subset_P}
\label{Complexity.NL_subset_P}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.NL, Complexity.NSPACE_subset_exp_dtime, Complexity.P, Complexity.logSpace, Complexity.mem_P_of_dtime_le, Complexity.spaceConstructible_logSpace, Complexity.succ_pow_le}
\difficulty{4}
Every language decidable in nondeterministic logarithmic space belongs to the
polynomial-time class $\mathrm{P}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Reduction to a nontrivial language]
\lean{Complexity.polyTimeReducible_of_mem_NL}
\label{Complexity.polyTimeReducible_of_mem_NL}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.NL, Complexity.NL_subset_P, Complexity.PolyTimeComputable, Complexity.mem_P_iff, Complexity.polyTimeComputable_const, Complexity.polyTimeComputable_ite, Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator}
\difficulty{4}
Let $L$ and $L'$ be languages of binary strings. Suppose $L$ contains at least one
string and omits at least one string, and $L'$ belongs to $	extsf{NL}$. Then $L'$ is
polynomial-time many-one reducible to $L$.
\end{theorem}
